findings.title: Raw encrypted values in `_source` are returned untouched when the `_id` column is absent.
findings.body:
`decryptSourceColumn` returns the response unchanged when `_source` is present but `_id` is not. That happens with `metadata: ['_source']`, or with `metadata: ['_id','_source']` plus `| DROP _id`.

`stripEncryptedColumns` only nulls columns named exactly `<type>.<attr>`, so it never touches `_source`. The full encrypted attribute ciphertext is therefore handed back to the caller. This contradicts the docs, which say encrypted attributes in `_source` are decrypted or stripped. The unit test at line 410 even locks this behaviour in.

Fix: when `_source` is present but decryption cannot run, strip the encrypted attributes from each row's `_source[type]` using `getEncryptedAttributes`.

findings.title: Agent scratch files (PRD and progress log) are committed to the repository root.
findings.body:
`tasks/prd.json` and `tasks/progress.txt` are working notes from an autonomous agent loop ("Ralph Progress Log", branch name, per-story `passes` flags). They are not part of the feature and add an unrelated top-level `tasks/` directory to Kibana.

Remove both files from the PR.

findings.title: The pipeline is not required to start with `|`, so callers can extend the generated FROM clause.
findings.body:
The only check on `pipeline` is a regex that rejects a leading `FROM|ROW|SHOW|METRICS`. The result is then concatenated as `` `${fromClause} ${pipeline}` ``.

A pipeline such as `, logs-*,.security* | KEEP ...` or ` METADATA _index | ...` passes the check. It becomes `FROM .kibana_x , logs-* | ...`, which queries extra indices with the `kibana_system` user's privileges. That defeats the point of auto-generating FROM from `type`.

The injected `filter` still applies. However, any foreign document carrying matching `type`/`namespaces` fields would be returned, and this turns on index contents you cannot control.

Fix: require `pipeline.trimStart()` to be empty or to start with `|`, and reject everything else.

findings.title: `_source` decryption uses the raw ES `_id` and drops `namespace`, so AAD never matches and secrets are always stripped.
findings.body:
The ES `_id` metadata column holds the raw document id, which is `[namespace:]type:id` (for example `index-pattern:abc`), not the saved object id. That raw value is passed as `id` to `decryptOrStripResponseAttributes`.

For single-namespace types, `source.namespace` is also ignored; only `namespaces` is copied.

AAD is built from type, id and namespace, so decryption fails for real documents and always falls back to stripping. The advertised decrypt path therefore never works; the unit tests mock the extension and hide this.

Fix: convert the raw id with the serializer (`rawToSavedObject` or `serializer.rawToSavedObject({_id, _source})`) to get the proper `id`, `namespace` and `namespaces` before decrypting.

findings.title: Encrypted-column nulling matches exact column names only, so a rename or EVAL bypasses it.
findings.body:
Encrypted columns are identified only when the output column name equals `${typeName}.${attrName}`. A pipeline like `| EVAL s = connector.secrets | KEEP s`, `| RENAME connector.secrets AS s`, or `| STATS v = VALUES(connector.secrets)` returns the stored ciphertext under a different name, and nothing nulls it.

The tutorial and JSDoc promise these values are "always replaced with null". Whether the encrypted attribute is mapped (and so visible to ES|QL) depends on each type's mappings, which I cannot see here.

Fix: reject pipelines that reference encrypted attribute fields at all, or document this as best-effort only. Do not rely on the output column name.
